name: Olfactory PE at Architectural Transitions
short_description: Olfaction is a transition modality with direct limbic access; smell marks thresholds, encodes emotionally vivid episodic memories (Proust effect), and signals material authenticity; rapid adaptation means olfaction contributes to arrivals not steady states
higher_order_principle: The olfactory system generates predictions about the scent of upcoming spaces based on multimodal context: visual cues (visible materials), spatial context (building type, room function), and memory (previous visits). When the actual olfactory input at a threshold matches the prediction, processing is fluent. When it violates the prediction, olfactory PE results — and because the olfactory pathway projects directly to the amygdala and hippocampus without thalamic relay (Herz, 2004), the PE is immediately emotional and memorial. Rapid adaptation (2-10 minutes) makes olfaction primarily a TRANSITION modality: it encodes arrivals and changes, not steady states.

neural_substrate.primary_pathway: olfactory_bulb → piriform_cortex → amygdala + hippocampus (direct, no thalamic relay)
neural_substrate.privileged_access: only sensory system with direct limbic pathway
neural_substrate.consequence: olfactory PE processed by emotion/memory BEFORE conscious awareness

olfaction_as_transition_modality.mechanism: rapid receptor and central adaptation sets ambient scent as new baseline within minutes
olfaction_as_transition_modality.architectural_implication: smell contributes to ARRIVALS and THRESHOLD CROSSINGS, not steady-state experience
olfaction_as_transition_modality.episodic_encoding: first breath in new space captures olfactory scene with high emotional specificity
olfaction_as_transition_modality.connection_to_TP2: olfactory change at threshold strengthens episodic boundary

three_sources_of_olfactory_pe.material_congruence: building looks like wood but smells like plastic → cross-modal PE → 'fakeness' signal
three_sources_of_olfactory_pe.functional_congruence: space is bakery but smells like disinfectant → functional olfactory PE
three_sources_of_olfactory_pe.memory_congruence: building smelled like cedar before, now smells like paint → stored olfactory representation violated

proust_effect.mechanism: direct olfactory-hippocampal pathway encodes odor-episode associations with high emotional specificity
proust_effect.retrieval: later encounter with same odor involuntarily retrieves architectural episode
proust_effect.quality: odor-evoked memories are more emotional, vivid, contextually specific than visually-evoked memories
proust_effect.architectural_implication: building scent profile becomes durable component of place identity

causal_links.evidence_base: EST (Zacks et al., 2007) — additional modality change strengthens boundary; Herz (2004) — direct olfactory-hippocampal pathway for enhanced memory encoding
Herz (2004); Herz & Cupchik (1995) — olfactory-evoked memories are emotionally vivid and contextually specific
Cross-modal integration literature (Spence, 2011); connects to MAT3 material identity
Dalton (1996); Sobel et al. (1998) — olfactory adaptation occurs within 2-10 minutes

scope_conditions: Applies to all buildings with detectable odors — virtually all buildings since all materials release some volatile compounds
Effect is strongest at transitions (arrival, threshold crossing) and weakest during sustained occupancy (adaptation)
Individual differences in olfactory sensitivity: anosmia affects ~5% of population; hyposmia more common in elderly
Applied fragrances (air fresheners, scent marketing) operate through similar mechanisms but raise distinct ethical questions
moderators: cultural_conditioning (olfactory hedonic responses are more culturally variable than visual; Majid et al., 2018)
ventilation_rate (high air-change rates dilute building odors)

design_principle.material_choice_is_olfactory_choice: natural materials (wood, stone, leather) have characteristic scent profiles; synthetic materials off-gas VOCs or are olfactorily neutral
design_principle.spatial_zoning: separating olfactory zones so transitions produce olfactory change
design_principle.threshold_emphasis: olfactory-distinct thresholds (cedar door frames, stone vestibules) mark episodic boundaries

interactions.nature: TP2 describes multi-modal context change at thresholds creating episodic boundaries. OLF1 adds olfactory channel with privileged memorial access.
MAT3 describes multi-modal material identity. OLF1 adds olfactory dimension: materials have characteristic smells that must be congruent with visual/haptic properties.
MAT4 identifies olfactory terpenes as one of five channels for wood-stress reduction. OLF1 formalizes the olfactory mechanism and extends to all materials.
T23 formalizes hippocampal context memory. OLF1 adds that olfactory input has privileged hippocampal access, making it disproportionately potent for context encoding.
